headline: Princess Kate’s new film talks about cancer and mortality. Here’s what to know.
author: Victoria Craw

paragraphs.text: LONDON — Catherine, Princess of Wales, has released a documentary about her experience with cancer, providing an unusually emotional and intimate account of her journey.

“Heal,” described by Kensington Palace as a “deeply personal” film where Catherine explores “life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort” in the face of serious illness, is a 30-minute film that sees her speaking to other cancer survivors and hiking three of Britain’s highest peaks to raise funds for a cancer charity.

The trailer shows Catherine, 44, describing her inner thoughts and feelings of vulnerability after her cancer diagnosis, in what marks a noticeably different tone from the British royal family’s previous guarded, “never complain, never explain” approach.
Here’s what to know about the film, which will air in Britain on Sunday, and on NBC and Bravo on Monday evening, before streaming on Peacock from Tuesday.
It’s emotionally revealing while staying carefully curated
Return to menu
In a trailer for the documentary, Catherine, who is still popularly known as Kate Middleton, describes how she felt when confronted with cancer and her own mortality.

“Cancer does change you. It changes your body. It changes you physically,” she said. “I think when you’ve had to confront your own vulnerabilities, when you’re faced with your own mortality, you have to accept that life is not infinite.”
“It does open you up; I think it softens your heart. And once you experience something like that, it’s very hard to go back to the person you were before.”

Heal. Premiering this Sunday. Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis. All… pic.twitter.com/jugVnF1qCZ— The Prince and Princess of Wales (@KensingtonRoyal) November 23, 2026

In the film, Catherine describes lying in a hospital room drifting in and out of consciousness and becoming aware someone was holding her hand, the Associated Press reported, after attending a private screening of the film.

“They weren’t talking to me. They weren’t trying to fix anything. They were just there,” she said, without naming the person. “And the presence of someone that stood by me in that time, I’ll forever be grateful for. And it really made me realize the importance of simply being alongside somebody through their darkest times.”

The comments are unusually revealing for Catherine, whose public appearances are typically marked by short interactions at official events. The film is also carefully edited and keeps several personal details private — it does not reveal information about the type of cancer she had, her treatment or future prognosis.
Previous royal generations have been less willing to reveal details about their health or private matters, and King Charles III’s own cancer diagnosis was communicated with a brief written statement.

However, Catherine faced intense speculation about her health in 2024 after she had abdominal surgery and retreated from public view. She later revealed she had been diagnosed with cancer, in a video statement that ended the speculation and offered support to other cancer patients.

The new documentary has been praised by cancer charities that say it will encourage others to talk about their own cancer diagnoses. In Britain, more than 400,000 people are diagnosed with cancer each year, while in the United States more than 1.9 million people were diagnosed in 2023.
Kensington Palace says all funds from the documentary’s distribution have been donated to support “holistic cancer care” at the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity,
It highlights Kate’s deep love of nature
The documentary shows Catherine taking part in the National Three Peaks Challenge this year. This involves climbing the highest mountains in Scotland, England and Wales, all within 24 hours.
Catherine previously has spoken about the importance of nature to mental health and her recovery, including making a four-part video series over the changing seasons.

In “Heal,” Catherine describes how she missed the outdoors when she was in the hospital. “Even when I physically couldn’t get into nature, I imagined nature from my hospital bed. And now that I’m well enough, I feel a deep longing for all those spaces, for the ocean, for the trees, for the mountains,” she says, according to a Guardian report of the private screening.

The Three Peaks Challenge also is described as an important part of her healing journey, and the trailer shows her striding up rocky peaks in high winds, looking out over the landscape in a baseball cap and grinning while wrapped up against the mist and rain, set to a soaring soundtrack.
Research suggests there are many benefits for mental and physical health from being outdoors, including boosting mood, improving blood pressure and cardiovascular well-being.
It features loving messages from her children
The documentary shows a glimpse into Catherine’s relationship with her three children, who appear in photographs but rarely are heard from in public.
When Catherine reaches the top of England’s Scafell Pike, her brother James Middleton, who has joined her on the climb, plays her voice recordings her children had made to encourage her.
“Remember, I’m always in your heart with you, and I love you very much,” says Prince Louis, 8, the AP reported. “And I’ll be following behind your back with you.”
Prince George, 13, says: “I’m tracking you on Flightradar up the mountains. … You look really, really strong,” adding: “Keep going, and we’re right behind you.”
“Hello, Mummy. I love you so much,” says Princess Charlotte, 11. “We are so proud of you doing your walk and your challenges.”
The documentary emphasizes the importance of family and community support, with Catherine saying at one point, “We’re not meant to carry life’s challenges alone.”
It shows her wrapped in a hug with Prince William, cheering on other mountain walkers and walking with James, who previously has highlighted their love of hiking together.

It also shows Catherine and other cancer survivors discussing their experiences, with Catherine saying, “I haven’t really explored this outside my family walls really, so thank you for allowing me the time to do that.”
